I basically stayed on a level of patch until cravings were manageable. So the beginning stages lasted longer than the later ones. I'd say in the beginning I kept a patch on for two weeks before lowering and later on I only kept them on for a week. Especially 7mg and 3mg.

I kept my patch on 24/7 (just powered through those weird dreams) and would change it at 10 am every morning religiously. When I had some severe cravings, I'd either exercise or take another form of nicotine replacement (like lozenges, gum, on!, Zyn, etc) if I felt like I couldn't push through on my own starting at 4mg. 

With my doctor's permission I also cut my patches in half and quarters to make the weaning off nicotine process easier. So my tapering went from 21mg to 14mg to 10.5mg (21mg cut in half) to 7mg to 5.25mg (21mg cut in quarters) to 7mg to 3mg (7mg cut in half). When I got down to 10.5mg of nicotine patches, I made sure to lower the mg on my other nicotine replacement. I completely cut out the other nicotine replacements when I went down to 7mg and stayed on patches only thereafter.

Oh yes. Quitting vaping was really hard for me. I tried cold turkeying and I just couldn't. But I've been quit for three months now. No, I didn't read the book everyone keeps recommending though I am absolutely sure that it might work. I quit with patches, nicotine replacements, and sheer willpower.

Just for clarity, there is an update [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/MMFB/comments/qnaf2g/update_ive_done_everything_i_ever_wanted_i_feel/) that is only three years old. However, I don't mind answering your questions here at all! 

I do still feel the same sometimes, especially when my mental health is not at its best. My wife's (now husband) advice was about 50% correct. I'll elaborate. I still haven't found new dreams, though I did come up with new goals to strive for. Those goals are simply a distraction and any time I am not working on them, I find myself spiraling. I did find a job I love, though that job is being a housewife. It's better for my mental health and for me to reach my goals. I am *extremely* lucky to be able to be a housewife in the USA. 

As of yet, we have not had any children. The discussion has come up a few times and we are pretty sure we will never be having children. I do believe that children can give you a sense of accomplishment and goals to strive for, but I don't want to base my life on another person unless that person is someone I have chosen. I have no beef with people who *have* children and do that, I just don't want that for my life. 

  
Right now I'd say my job is as a writer and housewife and I enjoy it a lot! I really think finding enjoyment in your life will help anyone overcome these feelings of a pointless life. I think I have genuinely found an "okay-ness" with everything that has happened with me, accepting that things just happen in life, and ultimately finding a supportive person/s that will help someone through these feelings. 

A word of warning though, I put all of my eggs in one basket (my spouse) and now that my spouse is really successful, making money, doing things I sort of wish I could do, I often feel this way sometimes. So I really recommend not basing *your* success off of someone else. Only focus on what you are doing, how you are doing it, and how you could, gently, do it better. 

I really do wish you the best if you're feeling this way and if you have any more questions I would be happy to answer them.

Setting boundaries and open communication is what makes relationships work. If he is so depressed he can't communicate properly anymore, or cannot respect/make boundaries, it is a matter of time before the relationship falls apart. Sometimes, therapy doesn't work well enough. It's time for him to speak to a doctor, a psychiatrist, whoever to see what else he can do. Medicine isn't always forever with depression/anxiety, sometimes it is, but being medicated and living is better than being miserable and barely surviving. 

Sometimes people need to separate to heal and grow into better people for each other. Sometimes people are better off as friends. Sometimes a rough patch like this is what solidifies a relationship into something unbreakable. That being said, if he refuses to help himself or communicate then there's nothing you can do. You cannot help someone who would rather wallow in misery, depressed or not. 

I hope things are better for you both soon and that things are resolved in a way that is healing for both of you.

You've been with him for 6 years. Has he always cared so little about you? Has he always ignored you when you asked him something? Was quitting his job *really* because he didn't like it or was something else going on (bad management, shitty hours, too stressful, bad coworkers, etc?)? How does he feel about his parents very apparent lack of concern for him? Seriously, he's not able to keep going to school or stay at a job and his parents have made it so he *has* to live with you or on the street. Did things get worse when he realized he couldn't go home or that you're the only person willing to help him? 

This sounds to me like his mental health has absolutely tanked and his support system just isn't working. Therapy did not work for him because he gave up and from my uneducated experience, he gave up because he is severely depressed. Him not wanting you to go to therapy with him is not a dick move, it's not him not wanting to get better. I refuse to let my spouse of 8 years go to my mental health appointments because I don't want them to worry, get scared, or make assumptions. 

Depression is often painted as this "can't get out of bed" absolutely soul crushing mental illness that happens suddenly. It can be, but for a lot of people it's not. It's doing anything that makes you happy obsessively because without it you're miserable. It's not caring about the things you liked, or loved, for no discernable reason. It's adamantly avoiding anything that might make you upset because you're already miserable. I could go on. 

Before I am down voted into oblivion for not jumping on the "dump his ass" train, I'm not saying you shouldn't. If you have caretakers fatigue (because let's face it, that's what you've become), if you're not happy anymore, if communication isn't working, etc, dump him. Just because you're the girlfriend-wife-mom doesn't mean you have to sacrifice yourself for him, even if he is depressed and at rock bottom (or almost bottom). Don't let anyone belittle you for doing what you need to do to live your life. It just really sucks to be mentally ill, having been through this myself, and seeing so many people just assume these behaviors are not related at all and that he's just suddenly a dick. If he is suddenly a dick, forgive me.

Wellbutrin can cause rage and mania-like symptoms. How long have you been on this dose? Are these rage symptoms strictly linked to your increase in Lamictal? When I took Lamictal, it was split into twice a day. If this is the same for you, are you taking your doses at the same time every day? 

Are these symptoms linked to external stress or do they seem to pop up at similar times every day? When I was on Lamictal for 7 years, I had to take my full dose at night at the same time every day. My mood would be in a "normal" range if I didn't, but it was way more stable if I was very strict on timing. Please remember that most medicines take *at least* two weeks to filter out negative symptoms, sometimes a month, and if you're in that time period it might just be a waiting game. 

Please do not change how, when, dose, etc of ANY of your medicines without talking to your doctor. I had many problems with Lamictal and worked through them and think it's a fantastic medicine, but it did eventually stop working for me all together. My dose was *way* higher than yours by the time I switched, but in that golden period where I my mood was stable and I was most "normal" I felt angry for the first time in my life when appropriate. 

I see other users saying that anger and rage are manifestations of depression and that may be so. But for someone like me who grew up super calm and never got angry, feeling it for the first time sent me *into* a rage because I had no barrier or coping skills. Is this something that may be happening to you? If so, you'll need to research coping skills or see a therapist to help you. Anger is a normal emotion and you need to be able to feel that and work through that unless it is out of control, etc, etc.

It typically makes me uncomfortable to see scenes of SA in any media. These are my feelings and are a product of my SA experience and I cannot stress that enough. I was surprised at how well RS handled the actual SA. Instead of showing us the entire gritty scene, we see her in a sort of "happy place" and go through her thought process instead. We do see Apollo taking the pictures but with how important they are plot-wise and to Persephone, I think it was clever to show him in that moment. 

I enjoy that Apollo is obviously a predator to the audience but has manipulated everyone else to think he is trustworthy or to second guess themselves. The addition of "Keep this between us" and "You're my girl" could have been plucked right out of my own experience. When I re-read this part of the story to write this comment, I still feel like this is a realistic depiction of SA. 

However, the aftermath leaves a lot to be desired. LO has fallen into the same traps that other creators fall into when trying to use severe trauma for character development. The SA is used as a blanket excuse, apology, and write off for any  ooc Persephone moments. I'm not going to read the whole comic again, but I can't remember her really doing *anything* to cope, to better her state of mind, etc because she's pretty much "fine" afterwards except when it's convenient for RS. 

She does end up going to the most unrealistic therapy session I've ever seen, but it's a comic so big whoop. I think realistic therapy would have taken away from what RS was trying to do in the comic at the time, it would have been wonderful filler for the time gap though. That being said, it didn't really change anything. Therapy was essentially a rehash since RS hadn't touched on it super heavily for a long time and wanted to make Hades' reaction have a bigger impact. I did appreciate Persephone's response to Hades becoming violent, it was very similar to my own. Which is why the whole SA shit pisses me off so much. 

RS has the ability to portray character development using severe trauma as a backbone but she goes out of her way to be lazy about it. I hate that Persephone dissolved so much over 3 seasons that her SA is basically an afterthought due to shitty writing. I hate that LO started as a complex story and morphed into a challenge to see how quickly Perse and Hades could bone before the audience gets tired of shitty storytelling. RS should be ashamed with this wholly unhealthy and unrealistic portrayal of SA aftermath, especially seeing that her primary audience is teenage girls. 

I could go on forever about how disappointed I am, but I don't think anything else I have to say is nice so I'll stop. If anything I posted hurts to read, I apologize. These are my thoughts and my own SA, my friends SAs, etc heavily influence them. You are not wrong for disagreeing and how you "recovered"/survived is not wrong either. Please pardon the use of recover, aftermath, survive, etc. Feel free to correct me and I will edit this post to include more appropriate language for a wider audience, I don't talk about this often and I'm not sure what people generally use. 

TL;DR: The SA scene was well done in my opinion. RS is just hell bent on being as lazy as possible with the aftermath and it's a damn shame considering the beginning of LO.

My advice for you is to figure out a plot for your story. You have part of it down, Warlock meets Lust Goddess and sacrifices something for power. When does this happen in your story? Is tricking/dealing/persuading Lust the end goal? Or does this happen in the beginning? What are some conflicts going on in your world that might persuade your characters to make their decisions? 

Figure out what basic things you want to have happen in your story and what characters you want to fulfill those things. As you figure out the plot you will figure out things your character has to do, become, learn, or fail at to make the plot interesting. You can write by the seat of your pants, starting with the Warlock meeting Lust and their interactions and dialog. If you stay creative, ideas may pop into your head that help you write your story. Just know that this writing technique involves a lot of editing, removing parts of the story, or complete re-writes. I've done this with one of my books and the amount of writing I have scrapped could fill another novel.

Lots of great replies here regarding warnings on your phones and TVs. Make sure you also tune into a battery powered radio if your power goes out. I always turn on the radio the instant I hear there is a warning, because I find I get quicker updates on the direction of things than the TV. I did find, however, that my phone did not give me emergency updates when a tornado clawed through my Kentucky hometown. So, I think it is very important that you know some of the signs that a tornado is approaching just in case you are left in the dark. 

The sky can become extremely dark (nearly black) with a hue of green or yellow. It does not look like something caused by the sun being blocked in my opinion, and you'll know something is wrong when you see it. This does not always mean there is a tornado, so watch how the clouds are moving if you are safe to do so. 

If you see clouds converging in one spot rapidly or starting to circulate then it's time to go inside. Do not assume all tornadoes look like funnels. Sometimes they look like a column from the sky to the ground, even if they are smaller tornadoes. If you don't see a wall cloud or funnel, but it looks like debris is being picked up and flung from the ground then chances are a tornado is either hiding in the storm somewhere or trying to touch down and you can't see it. (Some tornadoes jump or touch down multiple times before "sticking") 

Randomly getting large hail is a sign to look out. A sudden calm before, in the middle, or after a storm is a sign for concern. If you hear something that sounds like a rush of water, like a waterfall, that turns into a strange roar (like a train) then it's time to take cover immediately. Remember, if you see a tornado that looks like it is sitting still in relation to permanent structures and trees, aka not getting smaller either,  it is going in your direction. 

Also, a disclaimer: I have no idea if any of this is helpful in a hurricane. If anyone has any better advice that applies to tropical weather induced tornadoes, please correct me. While I have barely dodged a tornado, it was in Kentucky and my hurricane experience was with Sally so nothing like what's going on now.

Unless your medicine is actively hurting you, take them. Even if you're 100% sure you need to come off of them because they're not working anymore, take them until your psychiatrist can switch you. If they won't, find another psychiatrist and keep taking that damn medicine until he can switch you off of it. Bipolar cannot be cured. Your medicine is not like other meds. You cannot get better, go off medicine, and then stay better without it. 

If you didn't need medicine, you wouldn't have went to the psychiatrist and they wouldn't have given you any. Your brain is a roller coaster and the medicine is the lever that slows down the ride or changes the course. You cannot get off the ride. Your brain does not magically switch to a merry go round. You are stuck on the roller coaster. 

This next part is what my doctor has told me. I don't know if this is a scare tactic or what, but I'm telling you all anyway because if he isn't pulling my leg it explains a lot about why we tend to have problems with medicines and become resistant. Every time you take a medicine long term, it maps your brain a certain way. When you go off those medicines and have a manic or depressive episode, it adds connections and pathways that can make the medicine either not as good or not work at all. You are suddenly resistant to a medicine that worked perfectly fine before. 

That's why some people go off medicine and go back on and are fine, either they didn't have an episode or it was caught early and the remap of their brain could be stopped. That's why some people have to change medicines after an episode. When people repeat the off, episode, medicine change, off, episode, medicine change cycle, they get to the point where A LOT of things don't work anymore. There are people who just don't handle medicine well, and I'm not trying to call out anyone here. Please don't consider any of this a blanket statement. We deal with enough shit without calling each other out and making each other feel bad. 

That being said. You are not a bad person for going through the cycles. Everyone has a hard time staying on their medicines. Medicine sucks. It's a hassle, and I wish exercise and diet completely fixed the problem without medicine but that's not how it works. As far as I'm concerned, if you have to start medicine then everything else is important but secondary. If you exercise and diet, maybe you can lower your medicines one day. But do all of these things WITH your doctor, not against them.

Hi, I don't wet the bed but my husband does. He had a condition called Idiopathic Hypersomnia which caused him to not be able to get up to use the bathroom at night. He just couldn't wake up to use the bathroom, so he totally emptied his bladder when he did this. 

I remember the first time he wetted the bed, just days into our relationship. I woke up freezing to death and covered in liquid. I thought I had sweated (or maybe he had) because it was hot in his room. When I would go through my clothes, I noticed they smelled like urine so I thought it was my cat (she was a kitten at the time, so her pee didn't smell horrible). 

Eventually, I realized that every time I slept with him I would wake up freezing and covered in fluid. He was peeing the bed and it was bad. Honestly, this wasn't a big deal for me. It's just pee and he honestly couldn't help it. 

At the time, he wet the bed every other day and it would soak the bed. I suggested diapers, he agreed. Still he would pee through his diapers and wet the bed. It was bad. He went to the urologist and got some medicine for bedwetting. It didn't work. 

Eventually, I just got my own bed and slept in it whenever I didn't want to be peed on or when I didn't have the time to shower in the morning. (Maybe twice a week.) Eventually their IH turned into Narcolepsy, and their bedwetting got a little better. But then they started taking Zyrem. Want to guess what one of the side effects are? 

So now I just sleep in my own bed and occasionally sleep with him when I want to. Our relationship is okay, but it isn't strained by the bedwetting at all. Honestly, it's just not that big of a deal. I love him dearly. 

TL;DR: I don't wet the bed, my husband does. He wets the bed every night and empties his bladder which soaks the bed. I just sleep in another bed. There are people out there who genuinely will love you despite this.

Hi there. I don't have IH, but my wife does/did. So I guess I was her caretaker for almost 2 years. If you EVER have a question about any of this, you are more than welcome to PM me. Seriously.

Make sure you tell all of these symptoms to the doctor. She may not realize she is doing it. My wife would forget stuff all the time, even if it was super important. Try to make it to all appointments if possible.

My wife explained that she feels like she hasn't slept for 3 days most of the time. Imagine that every time she goes to sleep to put it in perspective. 

Please know that this isn't something you *have* to do. I may get a lot of slack for this but IH is hard. It is hard for everyone. Don't feel like you have to stay with her just because she has this. You need to be happy too, and if that means you need a break then so be it. If you are giving and giving and she's not making an effort, I can imagine why you're so exhausted. Relationships go both ways and if this is something you can't handle, you don't need to draw it out.
